question: Does the Phase 0 audit protocol discriminate a sound corpus from an unsound one?
blueprint_hypothesis: Yes - demonstrated against the retired dataset as negative control. Primary endpoint: gate verdicts on both corpora.

negative_control_integrity.why: the negative control must still be the file its audit was computed from, or this is a comparison against a moving target

modality_caveat: the retired corpus is tabular and GastroHUN is imaging. A gate that fails merely because a spreadsheet contains no JPEGs would discriminate nothing, so each gate is reduced to a criterion that is meaningful in both modalities and the headline count uses only those.

gates.name: Provenance, ethics and licence
gates.criterion: a named, citable source; documented ethics approval; documented consent; an explicit licence

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: Sci Data 12:102 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41597-025-04401-5; ethics CEI-2019-06-10; informed consent; CC BY 4.0 (licence discrepancy resolved in favour of Figshare)

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: no citable source, no ethics approval and no consent record for Peptic Ulcer_Dataset.xlsx (1269 rows); defect D10 records a re-identification exposure

gates.name: Physical integrity
gates.criterion: every record parses/decodes; zero missing, orphan or corrupt
gates.note: the imaging form of this gate is JPEG decoding; the tabular analogue is row parsing. Both are 'does the payload load'.

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: 1269 rows x 12 cols parsed; 0 unparsed dates

gates.name: Duplication and contamination
gates.criterion: zero exact duplicates; near-duplicate rule calibrated against a positive control before any count is believed

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: 0 exact (SHA-256) duplicates; 39,015,361 pairs scanned; 54 cross-split pairs flagged by an uncalibrated rule fell to 0 once calibrated against a synthetic-duplicate positive control

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: 0 exact duplicates, 0 excluding the ID column, 0 ID collisions

gates.name: Label architecture
gates.criterion: per-annotator labels retained separately rather than pre-aggregated

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: 4 annotators (FG1, FG2, G1, G2) retained separately across 23 classes

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: a single derived label with no annotator identity; defect D2 records that it was constructed by rule over the same text fields that become the features

gates.name: Agreement quantified
gates.criterion: chance-corrected inter-annotator agreement reported with intervals

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: Fleiss kappa 0.7475, Krippendorff alpha 0.7475, Gwet AC1 0.7475; all 6 pairwise kappas with patient-clustered CIs

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: a single annotator makes agreement undefined. The gate cannot fire, which is itself diagnostic: a corpus that cannot be scored on G5 has already failed G4

gates.name: Split integrity
gates.criterion: predefined splits with zero subject overlap and balanced composition

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: 0 patient overlaps across all three split pairs; class chi2 p = 1.00000; 0 duplicate filenames

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: no predefined splits ship with the corpus and no subject grouping key exists; defect D11 records the resulting contamination risk as unmitigable

gates.name: Statistical power
gates.criterion: per-class test-set precision adequate for the claims to be made

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: 22/23 classes exceed a +/-10 pp Wilson half-width; declared as limitation L1 and per-class claims restricted to exploratory

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: defect D7: 1269 rows across the target's categories leave no category adequately powered

gates.name: Population description
gates.criterion: age, sex and clinical context available for the cohort

GastroHUN (adopted).evidence: no age or sex anywhere in the release; clinical record coverage 60.21% of patients; declared as limitations L2 and L6

Peptic-ulcer corpus (retired, negative c.evidence: age 18-90 (mean 53.8), sex 637M/632F, indication and medication fields all present and complete

discrimination.interpretation: 6 of 8 gates separate the corpora, but the separation is weaker than that count suggests. Only 4 (G1, G4, G6, G7) are outright failures; G5 cannot fire at all on a single-annotator corpus; G2, G3 pass on BOTH; and on G8 the UNSOUND corpus scores HIGHER than the adopted one, because it ships the age and sex that GastroHUN omits. Gate-counting is therefore not a quality score: a report presenting a tally of passes as evidence of soundness would have described the retired corpus favourably on 3 of 8 gates.

fatal_defects.measured: maximum feature-target Cramer's V = 0.0614 across all 8 features; permutation test p = 0.7622
fatal_defects.why: no gate in G1-G8 measures whether the features carry information about the target. A corpus of pure noise with clean provenance, clean integrity, no duplicates and a full population description passes six of the eight gates.

fatal_defects.measured: the target was built by regex over the same text fields that become the TF-IDF features; dropping the obvious culprit column still left accuracy at 0.9165 because three other fields re-encode the same rules
fatal_defects.why: G4 fails the corpus for having no per-annotator labels, which is a different fault that happens to co-occur. G4 as specified does not test whether the target is derivable from the features, so a corpus with four annotators AND a circular target would pass it.

fatal_defects.measured: age uniform on [18,90] (KS p = 0.5366); categorical fields balanced to within 1%; 2 of 36 field pairs associated against 1.8 expected by chance; corpus vocabulary only 71 distinct phrases
fatal_defects.why: no gate tests whether the data is consistent with having been synthesised. Every marker here -- uniformity, balance, independence, a tiny phrase bank -- is invisible to G1-G8.

fatal_defects.measured: no comparable public corpus exists for the NLP framing
fatal_defects.why: the protocol audits the corpus in isolation and never asks what it could be validated against.

what_the_protocol_missed.finding: every defect that actually killed the retired corpus was found by the Phase 1.5 signal-and-circularity battery, not by the eight-gate protocol. The gates verify that a corpus is well-formed; they do not verify that it is informative. Those are different questions and this thesis conflated them until the negative control was scored.

proposed_protocol_extension.name: Signal existence
proposed_protocol_extension.criterion: feature-target association must exceed a permutation null at a pre-registered level; report the effect size, not only the p-value
proposed_protocol_extension.cost: minutes; the statistic is already computed in the Phase 1.5 battery

proposed_protocol_extension.name: Label independence
proposed_protocol_extension.criterion: the target must not be reconstructible from the features by rule. Test by fitting a trivial rule-based predictor and by ablating each feature field in turn
proposed_protocol_extension.cost: minutes; the ablation that exposed D2 is a dozen lines

proposed_protocol_extension.name: Synthesis markers
proposed_protocol_extension.criterion: test for uniformity of continuous fields, near-exact categorical balance, pairwise independence of clinically coupled fields, and a small closed vocabulary
proposed_protocol_extension.cost: minutes; all four statistics exist in the Phase 1.5 battery

verdict_statement: RQ5 is PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The protocol does discriminate: 6 of 8 modality-independent gates separate the two corpora and the unsound corpus fails G1, G4, G6, G7 outright. But the discrimination is not on the grounds that mattered. Only 1 of 4 fatal defects is caught by any gate, and that one (D2) only incidentally, via a G4 criterion aimed at something else. All four were in fact found by a separate signal-and-circularity battery that the protocol does not include. The honest conclusion is that the eight-gate protocol is a WELL-FORMEDNESS audit, not a VIABILITY audit, and the negative control is what revealed the difference. Three extensions (G9-G11) are proposed, each of which would have caught a fatal defect and each of which costs minutes.
why_this_matters_for_the_thesis: a negative control that flattered the protocol would have been worth nothing. This one changed the protocol, which is what a negative control is for, and it is the reason RQ5 belongs in the thesis as a chapter rather than as a remark.
